faq.a: Sharifa is associated with the Arabic form شَرِيفَة, whose core sense is sharifa; noble, honourable (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Sharifa?
faq.a: Sharifa is associated with Arabic. Sharifa is Arabic شَرِيفَة (Sharīfa), the feminine of شَرِيف, meaning 'noble, honourable'.
Yes — the underlying form شَرِيفَة is Arabic.
Sharifa can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sharifa should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sharīfa is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sharifa mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sharifa is rendered شریفہ and carries the sense شریفہ، بزرگ.

faq.q: What does Sharifa mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sharifa is rendered شریفه and carries the sense شریفه، نجیب.
A romanized syllable approximation is sha-ri-fa. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sharifa?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sharifa, sharifa. Script forms are شريفه, شریفه, شریفہ, شَرِيفَة, शरीफ़ा.

faq.q: Is Sharifa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
